[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-008-asyncapi-event-contract-standard.md#purpose-statement]

### Purpose Statement

This standard mandates that every **asynchronous (event) seam** between components be specified, at design time, as an **AsyncAPI 3.0** contract — the event-driven counterpart to the design-first OpenAPI mandate for synchronous APIs ([STD-APP-API-001](../api/STD-APP-API-001-api-design.md) §API-First). It closes the asymmetry in which synchronous APIs had a mandatory contract format while events had only .NET/Kafka *implementation* standards ([STD-APP-EVT-001..007](STD-APP-EVT-001-dotnet-kafka-consumer.md)) and no mandated *design-first contract*.
page_texts.5:
[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-008-asyncapi-event-contract-standard.md#scope]

### Scope

**Covered:** the requirement that each event seam be authored as an AsyncAPI 3.0 document before implementation; the document layout and per-message schema rules; producer/consumer accountability metadata; and the rule that a produced channel with no declared consumer is a defect.

**Not covered:** the runtime implementation of producers/consumers (governed by the .NET/Kafka STD-APP-EVT-001..007 and the messaging patterns PTN-APP-EVT-*); broker/topic operational configuration (STD-INF-EVT-001, infrastructure standards); synchronous API contracts (STD-APP-API-001 + OpenAPI, PTN-APP-API-015).
page_texts.6:
[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-008-asyncapi-event-contract-standard.md#compliance-level]

### Compliance Level

**Mandatory.** An event seam implemented without a design-time AsyncAPI 3.0 contract is non-compliant. This standard governs the **contract**; the existing EVT implementation standards continue to govern *how* producers/consumers are built.
page_texts.7:
[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-008-asyncapi-event-contract-standard.md#business-rationale]

### Business Rationale

Events are the seams that decouple services — and, precisely because an event has no synchronous caller, it is the seam most easily left unspecified: a producer emits, no one is contractually bound to consume, and the integration is discovered missing (or drifted) only in production. In a claims/enrollment platform this manifests as orphaned topics, silently incompatible message shapes across teams, and consumers built against an assumed payload. Mandating AsyncAPI 3.0 as the design-time contract — the format a broker-agnostic tool ecosystem already understands — makes the event edge a first-class, owned, verifiable artifact, realizing the **seam** decomposition axis of [ADR-GOV-011](../../../decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-011-architecture-pipeline-operating-model.md) for its asynchronous class.
page_texts.9:
[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-008-asyncapi-event-contract-standard.md#mandatory-requirements]

### Mandatory Requirements

- **REQ-001 — Design-first AsyncAPI 3.0 contract per event seam.** Every asynchronous seam MUST be specified as an AsyncAPI **3.0** document authored during logical architecture (the integration-architecture phase), before producer or consumer implementation begins.
- **REQ-002 — One document per producing service.** Each producing service MUST have a single `<service>.asyncapi.json` under `docs/design/seam-contracts/events/`, declaring the channels it publishes and the messages on them.
- **REQ-003 — Every message references a schema.** Each message payload MUST reference a JSON Schema 2020-12 definition; a shape shared across ≥2 contexts MUST `$ref` the canonical `_components/` library, not be inlined (see [STD-INF-DM-001](../../information/data-modeling/STD-INF-DM-001-canonical-model-standard.md)).
- **REQ-004 — Producer/consumer accountability declared.** Each channel/operation MUST carry producer and consumer identity as native AsyncAPI metadata (`x-producer` / `x-consumers`). **A published channel with zero declared consumers is a defect** (an orphaned event — built by no one downstream).
- **REQ-005 — Contract is the source of truth for both sides.** Producers are generated-from / validated-against the contract, and consumers bind to it; neither side may define an event shape the contract does not carry. The contract is authored before the implementing work items are dispatched.
- **REQ-006 — Versioned and drift-watched.** The document's `info.version` (SemVer) is its drift-detection marker; a breaking change to a message shape is a MAJOR bump and follows forward-only change propagation (a new superseding message/version, existing consumers not silently broken).
page_texts.10:
[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-008-asyncapi-event-contract-standard.md#recommended-practices]

### Recommended Practices

- Name channels and messages in ubiquitous-language terms owned by the producing bounded context (published language).
- Model message headers (correlation id, causation id, event id, timestamp) once as a shared `_components/` schema and `$ref` it from every message.
- Provide at least one `examples` entry per message so consumers and contract tests have a concrete payload.
page_texts.11:
[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-008-asyncapi-event-contract-standard.md#prohibited-practices]

### Prohibited Practices

- **Implementation-first events.** Emitting an event whose shape exists only in producer code, with no AsyncAPI contract, is prohibited.
- **Inlined shared shapes.** Duplicating a cross-context payload schema inline in multiple contracts instead of `$ref`ing `_components/` is prohibited (re-opens cross-BC drift).
- **Orphaned channels.** Publishing to a channel with no declared consumer is prohibited (REQ-004).
- **Bespoke event-contract formats.** Inventing a custom event-contract schema instead of AsyncAPI 3.0 is prohibited (defeats the recognized-standard, tool-ecosystem rationale).
page_texts.12:
[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-008-asyncapi-event-contract-standard.md#exceptions-process]

### Exceptions Process

1. Submit to the Application EA Lead: the event seam, the reason an AsyncAPI contract cannot be authored, and interim risk acceptance.
2. Approval authority: Application EA Lead; ARB for compliance-relevant event flows (e.g., PHI-bearing events).
3. Document the exception, expiry, and remediation in traceability.
4. Review each release until remediated.
page_texts.15:
[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-008-asyncapi-event-contract-standard.md#document-layout]

#### Document layout

- **Location:** `docs/design/seam-contracts/events/<service>.asyncapi.json`.
- **Version:** AsyncAPI `3.0.0`.
- **Structure:** `info` (with SemVer `version`), `channels` (the addresses events flow over), `operations` (send/receive with their `x-producer`/`x-consumers`), `components.messages`, `components.schemas` (or `$ref` to `_components/`).
page_texts.16:
[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-008-asyncapi-event-contract-standard.md#message-and-schema-rules]

#### Message and schema rules

- Every `message` has a `payload` that is a JSON Schema 2020-12 object (inline for context-private shapes; `$ref` to `../_components/<Entity>.json` for shared entities).
- Every message carries a standard header block (`$ref` to the shared header schema).
- Enums shared across contexts come from the canonical `_components/` library (no divergent value sets).
page_texts.17:
[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-008-asyncapi-event-contract-standard.md#architecture-constraints]

### Architecture Constraints

- **Constraint 1 — Contract precedes implementation and dispatch.** The AsyncAPI document exists and is approved before the producer/consumer work items are dispatched; `/eap-decom-spec-export-issues` halts on an event seam (a topic in the integration table) with no resolving contract.
- **Constraint 2 — Cohesion is verified at both ends.** `/eap-sdd-health-check` Phase 11 (Seam Cohesion) treats the event class as: producer served (real publisher, not dead code) **and** ≥1 consumer wired; a produced-but-unconsumed topic fails.
- **Constraint 3 — Shared shapes are canonical.** Any schema used by ≥2 contexts resolves to `_components/` (STD-INF-DM-001), enforced by `/eap-sdd-health-check` Phase 8 Step 3.
page_texts.18:
[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-008-asyncapi-event-contract-standard.md#technology-standards]

### Technology Standards

| Technology | Approved Versions | Configuration Requirements | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AsyncAPI | 3.0.x | one document per producing service; SemVer `info.version` | the mandated event-contract format |
| JSON Schema | 2020-12 | message payloads; shared shapes in `_components/` | per STD-INF-DM-001 |

Broker/runtime bindings (Kafka, RabbitMQ) are described via AsyncAPI bindings but governed for implementation by STD-APP-EVT-001..007 and STD-INF-EVT-001.
page_texts.23:
[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-008-asyncapi-event-contract-standard.md#phase-1-author-the-contract-design-time]

#### Phase 1: Author the contract (design time)

1. Identify each event seam from the logical integration architecture.
2. Author `<service>.asyncapi.json` with channels, messages, and `x-producer`/`x-consumers`.
3. Reference shared payload/header schemas from `_components/`.
page_texts.24:
[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-008-asyncapi-event-contract-standard.md#phase-2-bind-implementation-and-verify]

#### Phase 2: Bind implementation and verify

1. Generate/validate the producer against the contract; bind each consumer to it.
2. Confirm ≥1 consumer per published channel (REQ-004).
3. Wire contract verification (schema validation of published messages) into CI.
page_texts.25:
[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-008-asyncapi-event-contract-standard.md#validation-criteria]

### Validation Criteria

| Validation Area | Criteria | Verification Method | Evidence Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Contract exists | AsyncAPI 3.0 doc per producing service, pre-implementation | Review + `/eap-decom-spec-export-issues` halt | The `.asyncapi.json` |
| Consumer declared | No orphaned channels | `/eap-sdd-health-check` Phase 11 | `x-consumers` non-empty + wired consumer |
| Shared shapes canonical | Cross-context schemas `$ref` `_components/` | `/eap-sdd-health-check` Phase 8 Step 3 | `$ref` targets |
| Versioning | SemVer `info.version`; breaking = MAJOR + forward-only | Review + drift check | version history |
page_texts.26:
[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-008-asyncapi-event-contract-standard.md#testing-requirements]

### Testing Requirements

- **Contract Testing**: producer output validated against the AsyncAPI message schemas in CI (the `contract` test type — STD-APP-TEST-001).
- **Integration Testing**: at least one consumer proven to deserialize a contract-conformant message.
- **Compliance Testing**: `/eap-sdd-health-check` Phase 11 fails an orphaned or unserved event seam.
page_texts.27:
[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-008-asyncapi-event-contract-standard.md#documentation-requirements]

### Documentation Requirements

- The AsyncAPI documents themselves (they are the contract).
- Traceability from each event seam to its contract and to the producer/consumer work items.
page_texts.30:
[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-008-asyncapi-event-contract-standard.md#assessment-criteria]

#### Assessment Criteria

- Every event seam has a design-first AsyncAPI 3.0 contract.
- No published channel is orphaned.
- Shared message shapes are canonical (`_components/`).
page_texts.31:
[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-008-asyncapi-event-contract-standard.md#assessment-process]

#### Assessment Process

1. `/eap-sdd-health-check` Phases 8 & 11 across the service set.
2. Review event contracts for schema/versioning conformance.
3. Report gaps as release-gating remediation.
page_texts.32:
[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-008-asyncapi-event-contract-standard.md#monitoring-requirements]

### Monitoring Requirements

- **Continuous Monitoring**: CI contract-validates published messages.
- **Periodic Reviews**: event-contract set reviewed each release for new/changed seams.
- **Incident Reporting**: a consumer break traced to an undocumented event-shape change opens a remediation item.
page_texts.33:
[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-008-asyncapi-event-contract-standard.md#exception-handling]

### Exception Handling

Temporary (contract pending), permanent (rare; ARB for PHI-bearing flows), and emergency waivers follow the [Exceptions Process](#exceptions-process) with documented expiry and review.
page_texts.34:
[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-008-asyncapi-event-contract-standard.md#governance-oversight]

### Governance Oversight

- **Standards Owner**: Application EA Lead (Event-Driven).
- **Compliance Manager**: monitors event-seam cohesion via `/eap-sdd-health-check`.
- **Governance Body**: ARB for PHI-bearing or cross-domain event flows.
- **Subject Matter Experts**: Information EA Lead (shared schemas), Infrastructure EA Lead (broker bindings).
page_texts.37:
[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-008-asyncapi-event-contract-standard.md#example-1-a-well-formed-event-seam]

#### Example 1: A well-formed event seam

**Context:** Enrollment publishes `member.enrolled`, consumed by eligibility and notifications.
**Implementation:** the skeleton above — one AsyncAPI 3.0 doc, `MemberEnrolled` payload `$ref`ing `_components/`, two declared consumers.
**Compliance Evidence:** CI contract-validation of published messages; Phase 11 cohesion pass.
**Lessons Learned:** declaring consumers up front surfaced the notifications dependency that would otherwise have been discovered late.
page_texts.38:
[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-008-asyncapi-event-contract-standard.md#example-2-caught-defect--orphaned-topic]

#### Example 2: Caught defect — orphaned topic

**Context:** A service published `claim.rescored` with no declared consumer.
**Implementation:** `/eap-sdd-health-check` Phase 11 failed the seam (REQ-004) until either a consumer was wired or the event was removed.
**Compliance Evidence:** failing health-check report.
**Lessons Learned:** the "built by no one" failure caught at design time, not in production.
